units.text: ON THE MATCHING CONDITIONS FOR THE COLLAPSING CYLINDER
Introduction
In a recent paper [1], using the Darmois conditions [2], the matching of a general collapsing anisotropic cylindrical perfect fluid to the Einstein-Rosen (E-R) spacetime [3] is studied in detail.

As the main result of that study, it appears that the radial pressure does not vanish at the boundary surface of the matter distribution.The physical interpretation of this surface pressure is justified through the continuity of the radial flux of momentum across the boundary surface.

However, as we shall see in this note, such a result is incorrect.Indeed, a careful review of the calculation process indicates a mistake in one of the final steps.Once this mistake is corrected, the final result is the vanishing of the radial pressure on the boundary surface.This implies that any local pressure effect, predicted by a local characterization of the energy (momentum) flux of gravitational energy of the E-R waves, by means of pseudo-tensors (see e.g.[4] and references therein), will not be observed.
Let us show how this comes about.
